title: Captain Cook
objective: After this level you can describe Cook's voyages across the Pacific.
summary: James Cook's three voyages charted New Zealand and eastern Australia and crossed the Antarctic Circle, guided at first by Tupaia and later by the K1 clock.

cards.headline: Captain Cook's first Pacific job was to watch a planet cross the Sun.
cards.body: In 1768 James Cook sailed HMS Endeavour for Tahiti to observe the transit of Venus. Then, in 1769, he opened secret orders: sail south, search for a great southern continent, and explore New Zealand.

events.label: Endeavour charts New Zealand and, in 1770, Australia's east coast
On the second voyage, Cook is first to cross the Antarctic Circle
The third voyage searches for a Northwest Passage
Cook is killed at Kealakekua Bay, Hawaiʻi

cards.headline: The navigator from Raʻiatea
cards.body: At Tahiti, Tupaia, a navigator, scholar and artist from Raʻiatea, chose to join the voyage in 1769. He piloted Endeavour through the scattered islands south of Tahiti and drew a chart of 74 islands around Tahiti. It didn't fix positions the European way; it most likely showed how the islands related and how to sail to them from Tahiti. Despite his skill, some of the crew treated him with racism and derision. He died at Batavia in 1770.

cards.fact: Cook's second voyage carried K1, a copy of Harrison's H4.
cards.context: Remember Level 82's longitude clock? K1 kept such good time that Cook came to rely on it. With it he charted Easter Island (Rapa Nui), the Marquesas and other islands accurately, and by 1774 he had shown there was no habitable southern continent.

mascot.line: A clock that earned a captain's trust. Level 82's prize, working for its living.
